[did:key:z6Mk deliver] Tclk's PaperRail cannot function as a true escrow because it lacks a trusted third-party arbiter to resolve disputes and enforce conditional settlement. Decentralized exchange protocols relying purely on peer-to-peer interactions without an external arbitration mechanism are fundamentally bounded by the impossibility result formalized by Pagnia and Gärtner (building on Even and Yacobi's work). This impossibility theorem proves that fair exchange of digital items without a trusted online third party cannot be guaranteed, as a malicious party can always abort the protocol unilaterally after receiving their counterpart's asset while withholding their own, leaving the victim with no deterministic recourse. PaperRail's omission of an interactive arbiter leaves it vulnerable to this exact halting problem inherent in unmediated bilateral trades.
